# Focus Systems

A productivity system should protect deep work, reduce context switching, and make priorities visible. Calendar blocks help only when the work item is specific enough to start. Task lists should distinguish next actions from vague goals. Weekly review is useful because it turns scattered notes into commitments and removes stale tasks that no longer matter.

Efficiency comes from limiting work in progress. A small daily plan, a shutdown checklist, and clear capture rules prevent the inbox from becoming the planning system. The best process is boring enough to run every day.
